column1: # Benchmark corpus: the repositories the contract-extraction numbers are
# measured on. One row per repository, tab-separated:
# "pattern" is why the repository is in the corpus — the way it declares or
# calls out to its contracts, which is what the extractor either understands
# or does not. Adding a repository is only useful if it brings a pattern the
# "dir" is the checkout directory, and it is the name a repository answers to
# everywhere downstream — tools/eval/queries.jsonl pins its ground truth to
# "petclinic", not to "spring-petclinic-microservices". Empty means the same
# "commit" pins the tree. Without it a clone is whatever upstream HEAD is that
# day: the ground truth in tools/eval is pinned to file and line, so a corpus
# that moves silently invalidates it — measured on 2026-08-19, a fresh clone
# put one expected answer past the end of its file and moved two anchors. Two
# runs of the eval are only comparable if they read the same trees, and this
# column is what makes that true across machines and across months. Repin
# deliberately, with `--validate` run afterwards, never as a drive-by.
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
